text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after oil prices dropped on news of a potential Russia-Ukraine ceasefire. Crude oil is down sharply from recent highs—the gap between world oil prices ($125.44) and U.S. prices ($96.24) suggests crude supply concerns have eased—and lower oil prices mean refiners earn less profit on the fuel they produce and sell, even though U.S. refineries are still running near capacity at 92.7%.

The stock's sharp two-week climb of 15.6% was built on escalating geopolitical tensions that had pushed oil higher; today's dip reflects a reversal of that risk premium as peace negotiations appear to gain traction. While refinery utilization and storage levels remain relatively stable, the market's focus has shifted from supply disruption concerns to the prospect of normalized energy markets if the ceasefire holds.
